subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

The best of both worlds

options.text: The best practices in both, ancient times and present times
The best people on Earth and in heaven
An advantageous situation from two different things at a time
Being good in dreams and in reality

solution:
The correct answer is "An advantageous situation from two different things at a time".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate meaning of the given idiom is **"An advantageous situation from two different things at a time"**.
 
• **The best of all worlds:** When all the benefits of **two separate circumstances** outweigh any **drawbacks**.
 
 
• ***Example:** Ram got the best of both worlds in one car.*
 
 
 
• According to the meaning, the third option is correct.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Let's check the other idioms

 
 

 **Words**
 **Meaning**
 **Examples**
 
 

 **World of Goods**
 When you remark that something has improved **someone's life** or done them the world of good, you are implying that it has made them **feel better**.
 A vacation will be worked a **world of goods** for you.
 
 

 **Worlds apart**
 To be fully at **odds with one another or different**
 Our living conditions are **worlds apart .**
 
 

 **The World is at your Fingertips**
 This idiom can be used to describe **someone who has many opportunities available to them**.
 I have all the answers** at my fingertips**
